cast_dialogue.linea: The Present Perfect connects your past to who you are today. Your experiences are your treasure, heroes.
I've just started a photography course. I've already taken hundreds of photos!
I've visited Japan twice, but I haven't climbed Mount Fuji yet. It's on my bucket list.
I've already swum with dolphins in Mexico. I haven't run a marathon yet, but I'm training.
I've never flown in a plane, mis héroes. But life is long — I haven't finished my bucket list yet!

banco_oraciones.oracion: She has already swum with dolphins.
We have just started a photography course.
They have written a bucket list.
I haven't climbed a mountain yet.
He has never flown in a plane.
We haven't finished the list yet.
How many countries have you visited?
Has she run a marathon yet?
Have you ever gone skydiving? Yes, I have.
Has he visited Tokyo? No, he hasn't.
Have they finished? Yes, they have.

banner_diagnostico.opcion_a: I have visited Japan last year.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Use 'have/has + past participle' for life experiences WITHOUT a finished time. Signal words: ever, never, already, just, yet. Never use it with finished time expressions like 'yesterday' or 'last year'.

ejercicios.afirmacion: We can say 'I have visited Japan last year'.
'Already' usually goes between have/has and the participle.

ejercicios.texto_con_error: I have visited Japan last year.
ejercicios.respuesta: I visited Japan last year. / I have visited Japan twice.

ejercicios.instruccion: Turn it into a question with 'ever'.

ejercicios.pregunta: Name three things on your bucket list. What have you already done? What haven't you done yet?
ejercicios.respuesta: I have already travelled abroad. I haven't run a marathon yet. I have never gone skydiving.

guion: Sofía: Have you ever written a bucket list, Kenji?
Kenji: Yes! I've written ten dreams on it.
Sofía: What have you already done?
Kenji: I've visited Japan twice and I've learned to cook ramen.
Sofía: And what haven't you done yet?
Kenji: I haven't climbed a mountain yet. But I've bought new boots!
Sofía: Great! I've already swum with dolphins. Let's help Abuela Carmen with her list too.

comprension.pregunta: How many times has Kenji visited Japan?

reading.texto: Kenji has written a bucket list with ten dreams. He has already visited Japan twice, and he has learned to cook ramen. He hasn't climbed a mountain yet, but he has bought new boots for the adventure. Sofía has already swum with dolphins, and Ben has just started a photography course. Abuela Carmen has never flown in a plane, so the friends have planned a surprise trip for her next summer.

preguntas.afirmacion: Kenji has already climbed a mountain.
Abuela Carmen has flown many times.
